map.收缩率 = (受热前长度 − 受热后长度) ÷ 受热前长度 × 100%。热稳定: Shrinkage rate = (length before heating − length after heating) ÷ length before heating × 100%. Heat stability grades: shrinkage rate <3% excellent, 3%~5% good, 5%~10% average, ≥10% poor. Shrinkage temperature interpretation: ≥95℃ meets the chrome tanned leather requirement; 80~95℃ may indicate under-tanning; <80℃ needs stronger tanning.
A specimen 100.0 mm long originally and 96.5 mm after heating: shrinkage rate = (100−96.5)/100×100 = 3.5%, rated 'good'; if the shrinkage temperature measures 98℃ at the same time, tanning is complete and heat stability is good. A shrinkage rate of 12% with a shrinkage temperature of only 82℃ means under-tanning and retanning is needed.
map.收缩温度为什么能反映鞣制程度？: Why does the shrinkage temperature reflect the degree of tanning?
map.鞣制使胶原纤维产生交联，交联越充分、受热收缩所需的能量越高，收缩温度越高；因此它: Tanning crosslinks the collagen fibers, and the more complete the crosslinking the more energy is needed to shrink on heating, so the shrinkage temperature is higher; it is therefore the most direct thermal indicator of tanning effect.
map.收缩率和收缩温度要一起看吗？: Do the shrinkage rate and shrinkage temperature need to be read together?
map.要。收缩温度反映“何时开始收缩”，收缩率反映“收缩多少”；可能出现温度达标但收缩: Yes. The shrinkage temperature shows when shrinking starts and the shrinkage rate shows how much it shrinks; a case can pass the temperature while the shrinkage amplitude is large, so read them together.
map.收缩温度测定工具根据试样受热前后的长度变化计算收缩率，结合收缩温度评估皮革的热稳: The Shrinkage Temperature Measurement tool computes the shrinkage rate from the change in specimen length before and after heating and evaluates the leather's heat stability and tanning effect together with the shrinkage temperature, an important indicator in leather quality testing.
